chunks: Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar and 'Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'I have made the world between My servants a loan. So whoever lends Me a loan from it, I will give him ten for every one, up to seven hundred times, and whatever I desire from that; and whoever does not lend Me a loan from it, so I take something from him forcibly. If he is patient, I will give him three characteristics, such that if I were to give one of them to My angels, they would be pleased with Me from it.'

He said, then Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) recited the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Those who, when a misfortune befalls them, say: Indeed we belong to Allah and indeed to Him we will return.'
'Those are they upon whom are blessings from their Lord.' So this (blessings) is one of the three characteristics.
And mercy is the second, and guidance is the third.
Then Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'This is for those from whom Allah takes something forcibly.'

key_terms.الدُّنْيَا: The world, viewed here as a loan
key_terms.الْمُهْتَدُونَ: The guided ones, referring to those who follow the right course
key_terms.قَرْضاً: A loan, metaphor for worldly life or charity
key_terms.قَسْراً: Forcibly, referring to divine decree taking away wealth or health

ai.seo_question: What are the three gifts Allah gives to those who are patient when He takes something from them forcibly?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the dual nature of worldly trials as either a voluntary 'loan' through charity or an involuntary loss through divine decree, rewarding patience in both cases. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) explicitly links the three gifts of blessings, mercy, and guidance to Surah Al-Baqarah, highlighting the spiritual elevation of the patient believer. It underscores the Shia emphasis on *sabr* not merely as endurance, but as an active mechanism for acquiring divine proximity and guidance.

en.hubeali:
Abu Ali Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan, from Is’haq Bin Ammar, and Abdullah Bin Sinan, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> said: ‘Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Said I<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Made the world to be between My<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> servants as a loan. So the one who lends Me<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> a loan from it, I<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> shall Give him, with every one, ten, up to a multiple of seven hundred, and whatever I<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> so Desire from that; and the one who does not lends Me<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> a loan from it, so I<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> shall Seize something Forcibly from him. But, if he is patient, I<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> shall Give him three characteristics, such that if I<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> were to Give one of these to My<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Angels, they would be pleased with Me<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘Then Abu Abdullahasws recited the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [2:156] Who, when a difficulty befalls them, say: Surely we are for Allah and to Him we are returning [2:157] Those are they on whom are Blessings and Mercy from their Lord.
So this (Blessings) is one from the three characteristics, and Mercy is the second, and those are the followers of the right course is the third’.
Then Abu Abdullah<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘This is for them from whom Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Takes something Forcibly’.
en.sarwar: 21. Abu Ali al-Ash’ari has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar and ‘Abd ibn Sinan from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “The Messenger of Allah has said that Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, has said, ‘I have made the world a borrowing (place) for My servants. Whoever gives Me a loan I will return it ten times over up to seven hundred times over, and more if I so wish. Those who do not lend Me a loan I will take something forcibly from them. If they then exercise patience I will give three such rewards of which if I gave only one to My angels they would all become happy with Me.’

The narrator has said that abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) recited the words of Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy: ‘. . . those who when suffering hardship say, “We are the servants of Allah and to Him we shall all return,” [2:156] it is they who will receive blessing, [one of the three rewards], and mercy from Allah, [the second of the three rewards], and who have recieved the right guidance [2:157] [the third of the three rewards].
Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) then said, ‘This is when Allah takes something from one forcibly.’”
